issues.description: The parameter order of the teleport_s function is inconsistent between the template and the problem specification/solution. The problem statement and the solution expect teleport_s(circ, data_qubit, injection_qubit, p=0.0) (data_qubit first, injection_qubit second). The template declares teleport_s(circ, injection_qubit, data_qubit, p=0.0) (injection_qubit first). This mismatch can confuse students about which argument to pass and will lead to incorrect usage when following the specification or the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template's teleport_s function signature to match the problem statement and solution: def teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int, p: float = 0.0) -> int. Ensure the docstring and any example usage in the template reflect this parameter order.

issues.description: The parameter ordering for the teleport_s function is inconsistent between the problem statement / solution and the template. The problem statement (and the solution implementation) specify the signature teleport_s(circ, data_qubit, injection_qubit, p=0.0) but the template declares teleport_s(circ, injection_qubit, data_qubit, p=0.0). This mismatch can confuse students about which argument is the data qubit vs. the injection qubit when implementing or calling the function.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template msd.py, change the teleport_s function signature to match the problem statement and solution: def teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int, p: float = 0.0) -> int. Update any internal usage/comments accordingly so students see a consistent parameter order across problem, template, and solution.
